So I just bought my first 4qt slow cooker and it arrives this Friday. Anyone have any good recipes I should try out on it? I'm looking for things that don't require a great deal of prep, I'd like to set it and forget it and have a tasty home cooked meal to come back to. Anyone have any ideas?

Don't really have a recipe but pulled pork sandwiches cooked with a slow cooker are excellent. I buy pre-packaged seasonings for it at the store that taste great. Throw everything in the pot and let it cook on low for 8 hours. I've also cooked venison tenderloin with some salt, pepper, garlic, and onions that I really enjoy. I got my first slow cooker last year and it's been awesome.
Pork loin with chopped up onions and sauerkraut. Salt pepper and a little water or broth

My slow cooker is one of my favorite tools in the kitchen. The low heat and moist environment makes it perfect for cooking tough cuts of meat that need a long time to become tender, but there are tons of recipes that work quite well!

First and foremost, keep in mind that not everything cooks equally in a slow cooker. Sometimes a recipe that works easily on the stove won't work in a slow cooker. Pay careful attention to recipes that may require you to pre-cook any ingredients. Also, it is possible to overcook recipes in a slow cooker. If a recipe says 6-8 hour cook time, check at 6 hours and see if it's done, then every half hour after that if it's not done.

My favorite set it and forget it recipe: "Easy Barbecued Ribs"

Buy a rack of pork baby back ribs (whatever will fit in the slow cooker), then remove the membrane on the the bone side.

Rub all sides with your preferred dry rub.

Cut the rack in half, and stand upright in slow cooker, meat side facing out, around the edge of the slow cooker.

Pour a generous amount of barbecue sauce over the ribs (I usually do about 1.5 cups for a 3lb rack).

Set to low for 6-8 hours. It will smell just like bread baking!

Remove the ribs, and transfer the braising juices to a pot, then simmer to thicken. Baste the braising juices over the bone side of the rib and put under the broiler for a couple minutes, then flip the ribs, baste the meat side, and put under the broiler for about 3-10 minutes (until you have a nice caramelized exterior).

Done! Now enjoy the glory that is ribs cooked in a moist environment, juicy and tender.

I prefer this recipe because it really takes practically zero prep. Ribs aren't that expensive either, so it's great for lazy days when I want a great dinner with minimal effort.
